Title: US egg producer to cull 1.8mil birds after bird flu outbreak
Article:
Cal-Maine Foods said on Wednesday it would cull about 1.8 million birds after avian influenza was detected at one of its Florida facilities, forcing the US egg producer to temporarily halt production at the site.
The company said it has suspended production at the facility while following US Department of Agriculture protocols, and will cull 1.4 million laying hens and 360,000 pullets, representing 2.7 per cent of its flock.
The highly pathogenic avian influenza, commonly called bird flu, has led to the culling of hundreds of millions of birds over the past few years, disrupting food supplies and driving up prices, though human infections remain rare.
According to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), "the human health risk to the general US public from HPAI viruses is considered low."

Title: MCMC clarifies Nov 19 disaster alert system test
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has clarified that the test of the National Disaster Warning System scheduled for today is an internal technical exercise and will not involve public alerts.
In a statement, the commission said the exercise was intended to assess the system's technical readiness and was not a public warning test in Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Kelantan and Pahang.
The clarification
follows reports
about a live test of the Cell Broadcast System (CBS), which is being developed as part of efforts to strengthen the country's disaster warning capabilities.
The CBS enables emergency alerts to be sent directly to mobile phones within affected areas, without requiring recipients' phone numbers or an internet connection.
However, the system requires a functioning mobile network and compatible devices to receive the alerts.
MCMC said it would provide further updates on the system's implementation when necessary.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia, US to strengthen cooperation on sovereign AI cloud
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and the United States intend to strengthen cooperation in developing Malaysia's Sovereign Artificial Intelligence (AI) Cloud, with Washington indicating potential support of US$50 million for the initiative.
The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) in a statement said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and US President Donald Trump today announced their intention to pursue cooperation in support of the Malaysia-led initiative, including through the participation of US technology companies.
Under the initiative, Malaysia will determine the design, procurement and operational arrangements for the Sovereign AI Cloud.
"The infrastructure and the data it hosts will be located in Malaysia, governed by Malaysian law, and remain under Malaysia's possession, custody and control," MCMC said.
Potential areas of cooperation include technical assistance and training to develop Malaysia's AI workforce and strengthen the country's capacity to operate secure and resilient digital infrastructure.
MCMC said any participation by US technology companies would be subject to Malaysian laws and procurement procedures, technical and security requirements, as well as the conclusion of relevant agreements.
Under the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, both countries also intend to deepen cooperation in AI and secure digital technologies while fully respecting each other's sovereignty and regulatory autonomy.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: No to renaming breakfast marmalade! UK govt slams 'myths' over EU talks
Article:
LONDON: No, the UK won't have to ban smoky bacon crisps, and no, British breakfast favourite marmalade won't need to be renamed.
As Brexit wars return to the British political discourse, the government has hit back at claims fuelled by this week's crunch UK-EU summit aimed at forging closer ties with the 27-nation bloc.
In its "factsheet and mythbuster" released late Tuesday, Prime Minister Andy Burnham's government said it wanted to clarify "several points" about a package being negotiated with the European Union.
Friday's Brussels summit is set to focus on securing three agreements - cutting red tape for food exports, linking the two sides' emissions-trading schemes and finalising a "youth experience" scheme.
The UK government says the food and drinks deal alone could add £5.1 billion (US$6.7 billion) to the country's economy.
But pro-Brexit campaigners fear Burnham will push at some point to rejoin the bloc.
The UK voted by a knife-edge in 2016 to leave the EU.
In a reminder of the bitter Brexit battles which have plagued the UK, claims have been re-surfacing – mostly in the UK media – that the talks will usher in a new era of EU influence on Britain.
"Smoky flavours in crisps, sauces, and soups will remain on UK supermarket shelves," the government statement said.
And "British marmalade will not need to be relabelled, as most British marmalade brands on supermarket shelves already meet European labelling rules," it insisted.
It also stressed that a ban on small sachets of ketchup and mayonnaise or on single-use plastics like straws, cutlery and cotton buds was not part of the draft agreements on the table.
The statement also dismissed "largely speculative" reports that the UK would have to pay millions of pounds into the EU budget under the new package.
Burnham has committed to his predecessor Kier Starmer's "red lines" on Europe for this parliament, meaning no return to the single market, customs union or freedom of movement.
In a foreign policy speech Monday he said discussions about the long-term relationship with the EU beyond the next election – due by 2029 – would only begin after Friday's summit.
"The deal that's on the table will bring growth to the British economy," Burnham told MPs Wednesday during weekly questions.
"The truth is the Brexit deal that they negotiated wasn't good enough," he said in comments directed at the Conservative opposition.
"They've burned bridges with our largest market, old friends and neighbours. They just destroyed all of those relationships."

Title: IAEA says North Korea is expanding uranium-enrichment plant at Yongbyon
Article:
VIENNA: North Korea has built an extension to its original uranium-enrichment plant at its Yongbyon nuclear complex as it continues to expand its production of weapons-grade material, UN nuclear watchdog chief Rafael Grossi said on Wednesday.
The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) has not had access to North Korea since Pyongyang expelled its inspectors in 2009.
The agency now observes the country mainly using satellite imagery.
North Korea, formally known as the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK), has carried out several nuclear tests and appears to continue to produce the two materials with which one can make the core of a nuclear weapon - highly enriched uranium and plutonium.
"Previously, I have reported to you about the ongoing operation of enrichment facilities at Kangson and Yongbyon, the construction of an additional enrichment facility at Yongbyon, and the reported further expansion of the DPRK's production of weapons-grade nuclear material," Grossi said in a statement to a quarterly meeting of the IAEA's 35-nation Board of Governors.
Kangson is just outside Pyongyang to the southwest, while the much larger site at Yongbyon is further away from the capital to the north.
"Since mid-September 2026, a further extension to the original Yongbyon enrichment facility has been under construction with the new extension externally complete by late October 2026," he said, without elaborating.
"The ongoing expansion of the DPRK's uranium enrichment programme remains a cause for serious concern," he added.
Grossi said the IAEA has also "observed indications" that the 5-megawatt nuclear reactor at Yongbyon that North Korea uses to produce plutonium from spent fuel probably continues to operate and is  in its seventh irradiation cycle, after which the spent fuel would be removed for reprocessing.
Another, light-water reactor at Yongbyon has been operating since April of this year, he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: OPEC speaks up for fossil fuels at COP31 climate talks
Article:
ANTALYA: Efforts to boost electrification will depend on fossil fuels, OPEC Secretary General Haitham Al Ghais said on Wednesday at the COP31 talks, where host Turkiye is seeking to make increased electricity use a central outcome of the conference.
Turkiye has presented a target to increase electricity's share of final energy demand worldwide to 35 per cent by 2035 from around 20 per cent now as a way to curb climate change driven by carbon emissions.
But it has not specified that the extra power needs to be carbon-free, which critics say greatly weakens any impact it might have on tackling climate change.
Al Ghais also said electrification was not a panacea.
"While electrification is a core part of our energy future, let us also remember that it is also heavily dependent on oil.
"Grid expansion requires more petroleum-derived products and diesel-powered heavy machinery," he said in a speech delivered in the venue's plenary hall.
"While undoubtedly important, electrification is not the only solution to the world's environmental challenges."
Al Ghais said increased electrification came with risks, including cyberattacks on energy systems and possible issues with the supply of critical minerals.
"We will require all energies for energy security. We will require all energies to achieve sustainable development goals. We will require all energies to accommodate differences in national circumstances," he said.
The Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and allies, a grouping known as OPEC+, has previously caused upset at UN climate talks by backing the continued use of fossil fuels.
At COP28 in Dubai, for instance, it called on member countries of OPEC+ to reject proposals for any text under negotiation that targeted curbing the use of fossil fuels as opposed to emissions.
That conference agreed language on shifting away from fossil fuels, but did not commit to phasing them out.
Turkiye's own energy system relies on fossil fuels.
The hosts said on Wednesday that so far 75 of the nearly 200 countries attending the talks in the Mediterranean city of Antalya have backed the voluntary pledge.
The talks are scheduled to end on Friday, but, judging by previous COP meetings, they could go on longer if a deal has not been finalised.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man, 16-year-old son charged with murder of youth in Sibu
Article:
SIBU: A man and his 16-year-old son were jointly charged at the magistrate's court with murdering a 19-year-old youth in a fight at Taman Foochow, Jalan Gambir, earlier this month.
They were accused of murdering Ryuichi Hii Shan Jie about 12.30am on Nov 7 and charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which carries the death penalty or jail of between 30 and 40 years.
If the death penalty is not imposed, a convicted offender is also liable to receive at least 12 strokes of the rotan.
No plea was recorded from either accused after the charge was read out before magistrate Romario Jonoi, as murder cases fall under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
The court ordered the teenager to be placed at Sekolah Tunas Bakti, while his 42-year-old father was remanded at Sibu Prison pending the next mention of the case on Dec 28.
Deputy public prosecutor Mohd Syazani Izzaddin Abdul Muadzam appeared for the prosecution, while the accused were represented by lawyer Boston Ho.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Israeli spy chief lobbied for joint Iran strikes on US visit
Article:
TEL AVIV: The head of Israel's Mossad spy agency, Roman Gofman, advocated for joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran during meetings with US officials last week, according to two people briefed on the visit.
Gofman met with Trump administration officials, including CIA Director John Ratcliffe, in Washington, the people said, adding that the Mossad chief briefed the officials on Israeli intelligence on Iran.
Gofman also travelled to Miami to meet President Donald Trump's special envoy, Steve Witkoff, who has been co-leading US diplomacy on Iran and Ukraine, Israeli media reported.
The visit took place after Trump said on November 9 that he would hold off on strikes on Iran following a meeting with the prime minister of Qatar, which has been mediating indirect US-Iran talks aimed at avoiding a return to full-scale war.
A third person, involved in diplomatic efforts between the US and Iran, said that Gulf leaders have spoken to Trump asking him not to attack Iran, fearing Tehran would follow through on its threats to attack Gulf Arab states in retaliation.
All of the people spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to speak publicly.
A resumption of US-Israeli strikes on Iran would likely trigger a major escalation of the war, which began on Feb 28 with a joint attack by the two allies that killed Iran's top leader and prompted Iranian strikes on US-allied Gulf Arab states.
Gofman's meetings on Iran with US officials come as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faces the risk of losing power following an inconclusive election last month.
Netanyahu, now serving as caretaker prime minister, has been accused by political rivals of seeking to escalate the conflict to improve his weakened political standing. He denies this.
Netanyahu's office, which handles media inquiries for the Mossad, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
A White House official said Trump believed Washington's economic pressure campaign was so "devastating" to Iran that there was no need for "major combat operations."
The president, however, has all options at his disposal to ensure that Iran never gets a nuclear weapon, the official said.
The official did not provide comment on any meeting between Gofman and Ratcliffe. The CIA also declined comment.
In his meetings, Gofman briefed US officials on Israeli intelligence on Iran, the two people said.
One said the intelligence related to Iran's nuclear programme, a central focus of ongoing US-Iran diplomacy.
Around the same time Gofman was in the US, former Israeli minister Ron Dermer, a close Netanyahu confidant, was also in the US advocating for a joint attack in meetings with Trump administration officials, the two people said.
Netanyahu believes the opportunity to launch an attack is narrowing, they said.
One source said Israel was concerned the United States could begin drawing down its substantial military deployment in the region before the end of the year.
The two people said Gofman and Dermer's outreach to US officials was part of efforts by Netanyahu to convince Trump to launch a new attack on Iran.
A fragile ceasefire has formally held since April, though Iran and the US have repeatedly exchanged fire, including this week with the US bombing an Iranian island and Iran launching attacks on Kuwait and Bahrain.
In recent weeks, Trump has alternated between threats of escalating the war with new strikes on Iran and winding down hostilities, and US officials say he does not appear ‌to have made up his mind about how to resolve the conflict that has become politically unpopular.
Israel's military assesses that Iran does not pose an imminent threat to Israel, meaning that immediate military action is not necessary, the two people said.
The military did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Two European officials said that although Iran's economy was under pressure, there was no indication that the government was close to collapse.
They also questioned what the US and Israel could achieve from a renewed military offensive.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Heart-stopping sight: 2 children seen playing outside high-rise windows
Article:
SUBANG JAYA: Two children, aged 6 and 7, were spotted playing on a narrow ledge outside a high-rise apartment building here after they were believed to have been left home alone without parental supervision.
The incident, which occurred at 4.26pm on Nov 13, came to light after videos showing the children walking barefoot along the building's exterior went viral on social media.
Subang Jaya deputy police chief Superintendent Mohd Fairus Jaafar said preliminary investigations found that the children had apparently climbed out through a window before playing on the building's exterior structure.
"Both children are foreigners, aged 6 and 7, and are believed to have been left alone at home without parental supervision.
"They then climbed out through a window and played outside the building.
"Fortunately, neither child sustained any injuries," he said in a statement today.
Fairus said police received a report from a representative of the residential building's management at 3.11pm on Nov 16, following complaints from residents.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001.
Videos circulating on Threads showed the children standing and walking along a narrow concrete ledge outside the apartment windows, several floors above the ground.
In one recording, a child wearing a purple shirt and black shorts was seen walking along the ledge, while another dressed in white stood near an open window.
Another recording showed both children attempting to climb back into the apartment through the window.
The videos, shared by Threads user @thissoll__, sparked concern among social media users over the children's safety.
The post identified the location as an apartment at Tropicana Metropark in Subang Jaya.
According to the post, the building management issued a safety notice on Nov 13 following complaints from residents.
The notice reportedly warned that children playing on exterior walls, ledges and window structures risked serious injury or death if they fell.
Residents were also urged to alert the occupants, building management or police immediately if they spotted children engaging in similar dangerous activities.
Fairus advised the public against speculating about the incident.
Those who witnessed the incident or have information can contact the Subang Jaya police station or district police headquarters at 03-78627222.
Information can also be channelled to investigating officer Inspector Fatin Nur Nadhirah Zahari at 012-9979552.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries for next US House speaker
Article:
WASHINGTON: Democrats elected this month to the US House of Representatives nominated Hakeem Jeffries on Wednesday to lead them in the next Congress, putting him on the precipice of becoming the nation's first Black House speaker.
The incoming House Democratic Caucus nominated Jeffries in a closed-door, secret-ballot vote.
Many incoming progressives declined to say whether they would back Jeffries after the Nov 3 midterm elections, with several saying they wanted a leader who would support a bold agenda to pass populist policies that candidates campaigned on.
Despite some opposition, Jeffries is expected to be elected speaker, a powerful position that puts him second in line to the presidency, when the new Congress convenes in early January. The speaker election requires 218 votes on the House floor. Democrats will have a majority of at least 257 seats. Several competitive races remain uncalled.
House Republicans last week nominated Judiciary Committee chairman Jim Jordan to lead their conference in January. Jordan won the post over majority leader Steve Scalise after speaker Mike Johnson said he would not seek to lead Republicans in the minority.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thailand, Cambodia to hold third maritime talks in KL on Nov 24 to 27
Article:
BANGKOK: Thailand and Cambodia will hold their third meeting with the Conciliation Commission under the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) in Kuala Lumpur from Nov 24 to 27.
Thailand's Foreign Ministry said the meeting, organised by the Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA), would build on discussions held during the second meeting in The Hague, the Netherlands, particularly regarding the technical aspects of maritime delimitation.
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow, who is also Thailand's Agent, will lead the Thai delegation, accompanied by Deputy Prime Minister Pakorn Nilprapunt, who will serve as an adviser, the ministry said in a statement on Wednesday.
Thailand's delegation will also include Director-General of the Department of Treaties and Legal Affairs Songchai Chaipatiyut, who will serve as Deputy Agent, as well as officials from the Foreign Ministry and technical experts from relevant agencies.
The ministry added that Thailand, as a state party to UNCLOS, stood ready to continue cooperating with and supporting the work of the Conciliation Commission.
The first meeting of the Conciliation Commission was held in Singapore from Sept 14 to 16, during which both countries adopted the Terms of Appointment and Rules of Procedure to establish the framework for the commission's work and subsequent proceedings.
The second meeting in The Hague last October focused on the presentation of viewpoints and technical information concerning maritime delimitation, with Thailand providing relevant technical details to the commission.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Britain's Prince William visits Bollywood studio, watches dancers
Article:
MUMBAI: Britain's Prince William watched Bollywood dances and toured a film studio in Mumbai on the last day of his royal visit to India on Wednesday, while his wife, Kate Middleton, spoke to health workers at a maternity hospital in the city.
The royal couple, who are on a three-day visit to India's financial capital, will end their trip in New Delhi and meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi late on Wednesday.
William and Kate had separate engagements on Wednesday, with the prince visiting the office of a prominent Bollywood production house, Dharma Productions, in suburban Mumbai, while Kate visited a maternity hospital in the centre of the city.
William smiled and clapped as dancers moved to a number from Dharma's hit Bollywood movie, "Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham" (Joy Sometimes, Sorrow Sometimes), which is set partly in London.
Actors Saif Ali Khan and Kareena Kapoor were also present.
"He was gracious and kind and spoke extensively about the potential of Indian cinema and how cinema across all Indian languages is loved worldwide," said filmmaker Karan Johar, who runs Dharma Productions, after the visit.
[[nid:1580845]]
The royal couple have been on a whirlwind tour of the city of 13 million since Monday, playing cricket with the retired Sachin Tendulkar, visiting a craft school and attending the glittering award ceremony for the Earthshot Prize, a climate-change award that William set up six years ago.
The Princess of Wales, on her most high-profile overseas visit since receiving treatment for cancer in 2024, also presented one of the awards on Tuesday night, wearing a bright red Indian-style gown.
In his speech at the awards ceremony on Tuesday, William said the impact of global warming was becoming conspicuous, with repeated heatwaves and devastating floods, calling it a pivotal moment for the planet.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Endoscopy equipment spared in Kuantan hospital lorry fire
Article:
KUANTAN: A three-tonne lorry carrying endoscopy machines and equipment was partially destroyed in a
fire
at Tengku Ampuan Afzan Hospital today.
The Pahang Health Department said the equipment was not affected by the fire, which broke out at 4.15pm.
"The hospital's Emergency Response Team took initial action before the Fire and Rescue Department arrived and fully extinguished the blaze.
"None of the machines and equipment transported in the lorry was damaged in the fire," the department said in a statement.
It said no patients, hospital staff or the public were injured or killed in the incident.
The cause of the fire is still under investigation, and the department will extend its full cooperation to the authorities.
Earlier, several videos shared on social media showed the lorry engulfed in flames near the hospital's specialist clinic building, with thick black smoke billowing into the sky.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kuala Kangsar Form Three death: Anwar orders immediate probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed the authorities to conduct an immediate, thorough and transparent investigation into the death of a Form Three student at a school in Perak today.
In a Facebook post, Anwar said no aspect should be overlooked to establish the exact cause of death, ensure justice and prevent similar incidents from recurring.
He also conveyed his condolences to the student's family.
"May the family find strength and be granted patience as they go through this extremely difficult time. Al-Fatihah," he said.
Earlier, the Perak Education Department said it was closely monitoring developments and had
instructed the school to cooperate
fully with police.
The department had also arranged guidance and counselling services, as well as psychosocial support, for affected students, teachers and school staff to safeguard their emotional well-being.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Court reserves decision on Tan Kok Ping's appeal on defamation award to Penang CM
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today reserved its decision on businessman Tan Sri Tan Kok Ping's appeal against a High Court ruling ordering him to pay RM350,000 in damages to Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow for defamation.
A three-member panel comprising Justices Datuk Azizul Azmi Adnan, Datuk Aliza Sulaiman and Datuk Seri Latifah Mohd Tahar reserved its decision after hearing submissions from Tan's counsel, Datuk K. Kirubakaran, and Chow's counsel, K. Simon Murali.
On Dec 3, 2024, the Penang High Court ordered Tan to pay RM350,000 in damages after finding that remarks he made at a press conference on Oct 18, 2023, were defamatory.
The remarks, made in Mandarin, were translated as "incompetent", "ignorant" and "shameless".
High Court judge Datuk Quay Chew Soon found that the remarks, which were published by six Chinese-language newspapers and an English-language daily, had seriously damaged Chow's reputation.
In his submissions before the Court of Appeal today, Kirubakaran argued that the High Court judge had erred in law and fact in finding the three words defamatory.
He said Chow had merely stated the Malay translations of the three words as their alleged defamatory meanings in his statement of claim.
However, in his witness statement, Chow had expanded on the meanings, attributing to the remarks a more injurious defamatory meaning than that originally pleaded.
Kirubakaran argued that Chow could not rely on a more defamatory meaning than the one set out in his statement of claim, as doing so would be prejudicial to Tan. He added that Chow should be bound by his pleadings.
He further submitted that the High Court judge had erred in accepting Chow's self-serving explanation of the impugned remarks.
"There was an absence of evidence from members of the community or third parties or experts on Chinese language as to the meaning and effect of the impugned statement on Chow," he said.
In response, Simon Murali urged the Court of Appeal to dismiss Tan's appeal, submitting that the High Court's judgment was beyond reproach and contained no appealable errors.
He further submitted that the High Court judge had correctly considered the relevant facts and applied the applicable legal principles in finding that Tan was motivated by malice in making the defamatory remarks.
Simon Murali said there was no appealable error in the High Court judge's finding that Tan's defence of justification was unsustainable.
He added that the High Court had also rightly rejected Tan's defences of qualified privilege and fair comment.
Chow filed the defamation suit against Tan, who is the life honorary president of the Penang Chinese Chamber of Commerce, in January 2024 over remarks made by Tan concerning the sale of state land in Batu Kawan.
At today's Court of Appeal proceedings, Chow was represented by lawyers Kek Boon Wei, Lee Wen Qian, Fatimatuz Zahra Suhaimi and S. Sharanya.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Home is a dim hope for West Bank's displaced Palestinians
Article:
AFTER  Israeli forces pushed him and thousands of others out of the West Bank refugee camp of Tulkarem last year, Adel Darsieh held onto his hope of returning home, but it is fading fast.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has vowed no return for the displaced people from the camp near the northern city of Jenin, known as a hub for fighters.
He is now fighting for his political life after his party lost seats in Israel's general election last month and former general Gadi Eisenkot was tasked with trying to form a new government.
But even the prospect of an end to Netanyahu's rule is not enough to lift Darsieh's hopes.
"Whether it's this government or a new one, what does it change?" said the 64-year-old. "They're two sides of the same coin."
The Israeli military carried out a major operation in the north of the occupied Palestinian territory early last year, during a temporary ceasefire in Hamas-ruled Gaza, having vowed to root out extremists.
Shortly before the election, Netanyahu announced that no one removed from Tulkarem would be allowed back.
For Palestinian families, it is a second form of displacement. The Tulkarem camp was set up in 1950 for refugees who fled or were forced out during the creation of the state of Israel two years earlier. The West Bank has been occupied by Israel since 1967.
"Successive generations have lived through displacement without being able to return to their homes. If our grandparents and parents couldn't return, how can we believe that our return will be possible?" said Darsieh.
According to United Nations figures, the Israeli operation launched last year displaced 12,100 people from the Tulkarem camp.
With the Israeli military keeping up periodic operations around the region, Darsieh is living near the camp in a modest, makeshift home with a sheet metal roof. His wife uses a wheelchair.
He went to receive trays of mansaf, a dish of rice, meat and fermented yoghurt, prepared by Fazaa Kitchen, a solidarity group that serves food to the displaced.
Working from the building of the Wadi al-Hawarith charity, volunteers in orange jackets fill, seal and package portions of food in an assembly line.
The group prepares and distributes some 1,200 meals to 400 families.
"If we weren't cooking, families would be going to bed with empty stomachs," said the organisation's head, Hussein al-Sheikh Ali, 60, who himself is displaced.
He described Israel's actions in the West Bank since the Gaza war — a conflict launched in response to the unprecedented attack on Israel by Hamas on Oct 7, 2023 — as "collective punishment."
"Some Palestinians hope that a new Israeli government might emerge with a less extremist, more moderate tone," said Ali.
"Yet the fear remains that the same policies towards the Palestinians will persist, even if the political figures themselves change."
Faisal Salama, who heads Tulkarem camp's popular committee, which represents residents, called Netanyahu's decision to stop residents returning illegal.
He held out guarded hope for an end to military operations, pointing to how Israel, soon after the election, ended an operation in Hebron that displaced 3,000 Palestinians.
Even if residents could return, much of the camp has been destroyed. Houses have been razed, buildings emptied and businesses burnt down.
Eisenkot backs the existence of the major settlements but has also spoken out forcefully against extremist settlers who have attacked Palestinians with virtual impunity.
Beth Oppenheim, a policy fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations, said a consensus has emerged among Jewish Israelis on key policies on the West Bank, including opposition to the creation of a Palestinian state.
Still, she said Eisenkot as prime minister could be more flexible on allowing a return to Tulkarem.
"They would make the case that this is necessary to stabilise the situation in the West Bank and that having people displaced could create the conditions for unrest."
The writer is from AFP

Title: The real business of diplomacy at Asean Summit in Manila
Article:
THE first morning of the 49th Asean Summit in Manila brought a welcome gesture from Indonesia President Prabowo Subianto.
In his remarks to fellow leaders, he apologised to Malaysia and Singapore for the haze, albeit caveated with a no-fault declaration.
Prabowo spoke of Indonesia's considerable efforts to contain the fires, to no avail, and the punitive measures taken against the culprits.
His apology was more poignant for being made with the countries concerned at the same table.
Asean is often judged by the problems it has yet to solve. The Code of Conduct (COC) for the South China Sea remains unfinished, and Myanmar is still at war.
Some expectations of Asean are unreasonable. Its members differ widely in history, political system and interests, and the association was built to manage those differences, not wish them away.
The question is what the Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim makes of the opportunities Asean provides.
On the haze, Malaysia proposed a Sustainable Haze Fund to give regional efforts steadier financing, together with closer scientific cooperation.
Leaders also called for ratification of the agreement establishing an Asean coordinating centre for haze control. Malaysia will chair the relevant ministerial steering committee next year.
Energy came up throughout the discussions. The conflict around the Strait of Hormuz has exposed Southeast Asia's dependence on a narrow waterway.
At the leaders' retreat, Anwar argued for revitalising the Asean Petroleum Security Agreement so that the region can respond better to disruptions and urged members to buy energy from one another before looking further afield.
Across Southeast Asia, food production depends heavily on imported fertiliser, seeds and animal feed. Disruptions to these could threaten future harvests and push up food prices.
Canada's Prime Minister, Mark Carney, in a classic exchange on the fly, urged Anwar to make more of the opportunities Canada now offers, while dropping an invite to visit.
Myanmar was harder. Anwar has argued for sustained engagement with Naypyitaw, on the grounds that Asean can achieve little without channels of communication.
In Manila, the leaders agreed to keep Myanmar's representation at Asean summits and foreign ministers' meetings non-political, while leaving open the gradual restoration of full political representation if there is sustained and concrete progress under the Five-Point Consensus.
Asean's limitations are part of the reason it remains necessary. Each member would have to manage its disputes and its dealings with the major powers largely alone, especially in relations with China and the United States.
Both are essential to Southeast Asia's economic future, though their interests do not always coincide with ours.
At the Asean-China Summit, Malaysia delivered two statements: the first on behalf of Asean, whose relations with Beijing it coordinates, and the second in its own name.
The national statement welcomed the upgraded Asean-China Free Trade Agreement while insisting on balanced trade.
Collaboration in advancing digital transformation should be enhanced "particularly in forging the upward trajectory of artificial intelligence", and strengthening governance frameworks and regulatory guardrails.
The intervention also addressed the South China Sea, where Malaysia co-chairs the COC negotiations with China, and called for renewed political will to conclude an agreement.
Closer economic cooperation with Beijing and the defence of Malaysia's maritime rights can be pursued together, provided difficulties in one area are not allowed to block progress in the other.
At the Asean-United Nations Summit, Malaysia argued that a rules-based international order cannot endure under selective morality, and reiterated the call for Security Council reform, including abolition of the veto.
Its position on Palestine has been equally consistent. Principles are of little use if they change according to the company one keeps.
The summit made plain how much diplomacy concerns matters that once seemed domestic. Electricity supply, food prices and the security of supply chains are increasingly shaped by decisions taken abroad.
Malaysia can work with others to reduce its vulnerabilities and widen its choices.
I have attended enough of these meetings to be wary of claiming too much for Asean.
But I am just as tired of doubting Thomases who are hell-bent on denigrating Asean centrality as sheer nonsense.
Asean cannot settle every dispute or protect its members from every external shock. But it gives countries that often disagree a reason to keep working together, and firmer ground for dealing with the wider world.

Title: NST Leader: Malaysia must draw tourists beyond KL, Penang and Johor Baru
Article:
WHAT makes a nation a historically great tourist destination that it consistently draws scores of millions of international visitors? To be sure, it comes down to a combination of natural beauty, cultural depth, reliable infrastructure, safety and value for money.
That's why places like Thailand's Phuket and Indonesia's Bali are famous attractions — island paradises renowned for their living culture and world-class wellness and retreats.
Then there are the nations that, though not exactly cheap, stand out — like Japan, ranked first in the World Economic Forum's 2026 Travel & Tourism Development Index, and Spain, which combines world-class cultural landmarks, culinary traditions and Mediterranean coastlines.
Of course, London, New York and Paris are the premier urban tourism powerhouses offering cultural depth and global connectivity while competing on iconic recognition and experiential depth rather than value.
What about Malaysia? It is ranked 26th in the index and is among the world's five fastest-improving tourism economies alongside Albania, Vietnam, Laos and Qatar.
Buoyed by the Visit Malaysia 2026 campaign — so successful that it has been extended to 2027 — Malaysia led Southeast Asia with 42.2 million international visitors in 2025 and recorded 32.26 million arrivals in the first nine months of this year.
Malaysia's big advantage lies in its affordable pricing on dining, transit, high-end hotels, ultra-modern shopping malls and top-notch medical facilities.
The blend of Malay, Chinese, Indian and indigenous heritage is a melting pot of cultural identity, drawing visitors to world heritage cities like George Town and Melaka. Malaysia pairs ancient rainforests and wildlife sanctuaries with cool highland retreats.
Kuala Lumpur is a major regional aviation hub, with extensive air links across Asia, the Middle East and Europe, coupled with gleaming highways, rail networks and widespread English proficiency.
Recognising the opportunity, the government will spend RM2 million to upgrade decorative lighting along Jalan Bukit Bintang in conjunction with the 70 Years of Malaysian Excellence celebrations next year.
Besides boosting Kuala Lumpur's appeal as a night-time tourism destination, the I Lite U 2.0 urban lighting project supports Malaysia's target of 47 million international arrivals and RM329 billion in tourism receipts for Visit Malaysia 2026. Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming described the I Lite U 2.0 urban lighting project as designed to enhance Bukit Bintang's night-time appeal.
Therein lies the rub: we also need to move beyond the traditional marketing of Kuala Lumpur, Penang and Johor Baru and disperse tourists to the East Coast, Sabah and Sarawak.
This means improving last-mile connectivity, upgrading digital booking platforms for rural operators and enhancing storytelling at heritage and natural sites that turns brief stopovers into compelling itineraries.
Equally important is protecting the very assets that attract travellers. The warning signs are already evident in Europe from unchecked over-tourism and environmental degradation at marine parks to declining service standards.
To avoid an erosion of appeal, industry players must enforce stricter sustainability standards, maintain public cleanliness and invest in hospitality training. Malaysia has a proven global tourism record, but the long-term mission is to ensure visitors stay longer, spend deeper and leave as ambassadors.

Title: Don't panic if your phone alarm goes off tomorrow, it's only a drill
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The national Cell Broadcast System (CBS), designed to deliver disaster warnings directly to mobile phones, will undergo live testing tomorrow.
Developed by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), the system will send alerts to mobile phones in affected areas without requiring recipients' phone numbers, SMS services or an internet connection.
It is intended to complement and eventually replace the existing SMS-based disaster warning system, allowing faster and more targeted alerts to people in areas at risk.
The system broadcasts alerts through mobile networks to compatible devices within designated areas. It requires at least one functioning mobile network in the affected area, regardless of the recipient's service provider.
The pilot exercise is expected to focus on flood-prone areas, including Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Kelantan and Pahang.
The National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) has confirmed that the testing will take place tomorrow.
Posters circulating on social media have reminded the public not to panic if their mobile phones emit a loud siren and display an evacuation alert during the exercise, as it is only a drill.
Previously, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said
timely warnings
could give people valuable minutes to evacuate and seek shelter before disaster struck.
"Through this system, warnings can be sent directly to mobile phones in areas at risk without interfering with or accessing personal data," he said.

Title: AI growth must be backed by safeguards, support structures
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The government is committed to strengthening policies, support structures and high-speed digital infrastructure to protect Malaysians while ensuring the country fully harnesses the economic benefits of artificial intelligence (AI), said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said the government was taking a deliberate and purposeful approach to governance to ensure adequate safeguards for citizens as AI transforms industries and reshapes the employment landscape.
"We have got to make sure for the government, that our policies and regulations, that the kind of safety and support structures can withstand the kind of creative destruction or the creation of new jobs that we will see in the next five years.
"Because of AI and how AI changes the way some businesses, some industries, some sectors work," he said during a panel session titled "The AI Wave, Malaysia's Next Move" at the Putrajaya Festival of Ideas (FOI) 2026.
Fahmi likened the government's role to the "Hobbesian Leviathan", a concept introduced by political philosopher Thomas Hobbes that describes a powerful state authority entrusted with maintaining order and protecting society.
Drawing on the concept, he said rapid technological developments required careful consideration rather than hasty legislation, adding that the government's measured approach to regulation was intended to provide lasting protection for the people.
"It's something (regulations drafting) that moves very slowly, purposefully, but it is to provide sanctuary for the populace, for people," he said.
He acknowledged the challenges of regulating AI, given the pace at which the technology evolves, noting that the legislative process could take considerable time.
"So, there's always this question: you will find it very hard to regulate because you don't know how AI will reinvent itself three months from now, six months from now. To pass a law in Parliament takes a ministry two years," he added.
On institutional efforts, Fahmi highlighted the establishment of AI Malaysia Bhd as one of the concrete steps taken by the Madani government to strengthen the country's AI ecosystem.
He said Malaysia was also in an unique position to attract economic opportunities from the expansion of data centres, although two countries currently account for 90 per cent of global AI computing capacity.
Fahmi said the government's sustained efforts over the past four years to expand 5G connectivity had also laid a strong foundation for wider AI adoption, with coverage reaching about 92 per cent and adoption at 89 per cent.
He said the connectivity would enable businesses, communities and students to make productive use of AI tools and contribute to national economic growth.
Emphasising the need for prudent management of public funds, Fahmi said government incentives and initiatives to encourage AI adoption must be guided by evidence to ensure they deliver tangible benefits.
"Things so that we are not wasting people's money to encourage people to use AI for things that they might not actually see," he said.

Title: Wan Rosdy calls for probe into Pua's disclosure of Pardons Board minutes
Article:
KUANTAN: The disclosure of purported Pardons Board meeting minutes concerning Datuk Seri Najib Abdul Razak's house arrest order by former DAP lawmaker Tony Pua has raised concerns over the confidentiality and security of government records.
Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail said the disclosure raised questions about the handling and governance of official documents.
"How could documents relating to the official proceedings of the Pardons Board be made public? Who was responsible for safeguarding these documents, and what procedures were followed before they were declassified?
"I urge the authorities to investigate the matter, including possible violations of laws relating to 3R issues (race, religion and royalty), as well as breaches involving the security and confidentiality of government documents.
"If any laws or procedures have been breached, action must be taken without fear or favour," he said in a statement today.
Wan Rosdy said political differences should not be used to undermine the dignity of the Royal Institutions, adding that respecting the Yang di-Pertuan Agong and protecting confidential government documents were matters of principle, law and national responsibility.
He also accused Pua of showing disrespect towards the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, saying the Royal Institutions should not be drawn into political controversies.
"We must never allow a situation where 'kaduk naik junjung' (abusing one's freedom), to the extent that people forget the limits, decorum and responsibility required to respect the country's institutions," he said.
Earlier today, Pua uploaded a series of images on his Facebook page, claiming that the minutes of the Pardons Board meeting concerning Najib's house arrest order had been declassified.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sri Maha Mariamman Temple clarifies Anwar, Macron did not enter inner sanctum with shoes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The management of Sri Maha Mariamman Temple here has dismissed claims of religious disrespect following an unscheduled visit by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and French President Emmanuel Macron yesterday, clarifying that the leaders did not enter the temple's inner sanctum.
Temple chairman Tan Sri Dr R. Nadarajah said the brief stopover was unplanned, with the management receiving no prior notification from the authorities or organisers.
"We did not even know they were coming. I was at the hospital at the time, and neither the secretary, treasurer nor any trustees were present at the temple to receive them or advise on footwear protocol," he told Bernama when contacted today.
He was responding to statements issued earlier today by the Malaysia Hindu Sangam (MHS) and Malaysia Hindu Dharma Mamandram, which questioned the wearing of shoes by the two leaders and their delegation during a walkabout near Petaling Street.
Nadarajah explained that Anwar, Macron and their entourage had only stepped onto the front verandah beneath the rajagopuram (main entrance tower) and did not enter the main prayer hall or sannidhanam (inner sanctum), where footwear is strictly prohibited.
"Nobody can enter the inner sanctum wearing shoes. They merely stepped into the outer verandah area while walking past," he said.
He added that temple workers on duty could not reasonably be expected to intercept high-level security personnel and foreign dignitaries in the absence of the management.
Expressing his delight over the visit, Nadarajah said the temple was honoured to welcome both leaders, who were also visibly pleased to visit the house of worship.
He urged all parties not to blow the matter out of proportion.
Yesterday, Anwar took Macron on an
informal walkabout
around the Petaling Street heritage enclave, including brief stops at Guan Di Temple and Sri Maha Mariamman Temple, in conjunction with the French leader's 2-day official visit to Malaysia.

Title: Zahid prays for recovery of policemen injured in Tapah crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has prayed for the recovery of policemen injured in an accident in Tapah, Perak, yesterday.
In a Facebook post today, he also prayed that the families of those involved would be granted the strength to endure this trying time.
Zahid said he had been briefed on the condition of those currently receiving treatment at Slim River Hospital, including Lance Corporal Ridzuan Sarizan from the Bagan Datuk district police headquarters.
"Let us all pray that he and all the injured personnel have a smooth medical treatment and are granted a full recovery," he said.
Zahid, who is also Bagan Datuk member of parliament, said his political secretary, Datuk Abdul Aziz Julkarnain, visited several of the personnel undergoing treatment at Slim River Hospital today on his behalf.
He said Aziz is scheduled to travel to Tumpat, Kelantan, tomorrow to visit the family of the late Lance Corporal Muhammad Shahrul Alif Yaacob, who died in the incident.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said that four of the 10 policemen injured in the accident have been discharged from Tapah Hospital while the remaining six are still receiving treatment at three different facilities namely Slim River Hospital, Tapah Hospital, and Teluk Intan Hospital with all reported to be in stable condition.
A Maxus van driven by a policeman and carrying 10 passengers crashed into a highway steel barrier after its rear left tyre burst.
The
crash
claimed the life of Shahrul Alif, 26, who was stationed at the Batu Gajah district police headquarters.

Title: Flash floods hit Puncak Alam, Meru for second consecutive night
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Flash floods struck parts of Puncak Alam for the second consecutive day today, with several roads inundated following heavy rain this evening.
Videos and photographs circulating on social media showed floodwaters covering roads near a fast food outlet and a traffic light junction in Puncak Alam.
A Threads user, @frhanirhmn, shared footage of the flooding at 8.16pm, showing muddy floodwaters covering sections of the road.
The flooding affected Jalan Bukit Cherakah heading towards Meru, where another video showed vehicles navigating a waterlogged stretch.
The same user later posted an update indicating that rain had resumed in the area.
The latest flooding comes a day after heavy rain triggered flash floods at several locations in Puncak Alam, including Jalan Bukit Cherakah heading towards Meru, where rising floodwaters caused traffic congestion.
Meanwhile, flooding was also reported in Meru, Klang, tonight.
A Threads user, @izzi5935, shared photographs and aerial footage showing extensive flooding at Taman Daya Maju in Meru.
The images showed roads submerged in muddy floodwaters, with water surrounding houses and other buildings in the residential neighbourhood.
The user claimed in the post that some affected residents had only received flood assistance from a non-governmental organisation earlier this evening.
Another video shared by Threads user @along_sam showed floodwaters rising in Batu Arang, with a pick-up truck navigating the inundated road as heavy rain continued.
Motorists travelling through Puncak Alam and Meru are advised to exercise caution, avoid flooded roads and use alternative routes where necessary.
Floodwaters can be dangerous as their depth may be difficult to gauge, while strong currents, submerged obstacles and open drains pose risks to motorists and pedestrians.
The full extent of the flooding and the number of affected households have yet to be established.
Meanwhile, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) issued a thunderstorm warning at 8.45pm today, forecasting thunderstorms and heavy rain across several states until midnight.
The warning covers Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, as well as parts of Kedah, Perak, Pahang, Negri Sembilan, Johor and Sarawak.
In Kedah, the affected areas include Langkawi, Sik, Padang Terap and Baling, while in Perak, the warning covers Manjung, Perak Tengah, Bagan Datuk and Hilir Perak.
In Pahang, thunderstorms and heavy rain are expected in Rompin, Bera, Temerloh, Bentong and Raub.
The warning also covers Seremban, Rembau, Jelebu, Jempol, Kuala Pilah and Port Dickson in Negri Sembilan, as well as Kota Tinggi and Mersing in Johor.
In Sarawak, the affected areas are Belaga, Kapit and Bukit Mabong in the Kapit division, along with Tatau and Sebauh in Bintulu.
The warning remains in effect until midnight on Nov 19.

Title: Sultan Sharafuddin impressed by Merdeka Textile Museum
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, has expressed admiration for the establishment of the Merdeka Textile Museum and its role in preserving and showcasing the rich textile heritage of the Malay world.
In a Selangor Royal Office Facebook post, Sultan Sharafuddin said he was particularly impressed by the museum's curatorial standards and the meticulous arrangement and presentation of its collection of fabrics, traditional attire and textiles.
His Royal Highness was also drawn to the museum's efforts to showcase the intricacy of traditional craftsmanship and explore the history, culture and identity of the Malay and Nusantara communities through textiles.
"I am greatly impressed by the establishment of the Merdeka Textile Museum and its role in highlighting the history, artistry and craftsmanship of traditional Malay textiles.
"I had hoped that a similar textile museum would have been established in Selangor by now, but I am disappointed that this has yet to materialise," the Sultan said.
Yesterday, Sultan Sharafuddin, accompanied by Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin, spent almost two hours touring the museum, which was officially launched on Aug 21.
Among the exhibits that particularly fascinated the Sultan was the personal collection of the late cultural figure Azah Aziz, which forms the core of the museum's collection.
Donated by her family, the collection comprises 240 pieces of traditional attire and 69 traditional accessories, including songket sarongs, baju kurung limar and gold-thread embroidery, preserving her legacy in safeguarding Malay traditional clothing heritage.
Located at Look at 118, within the Merdeka 118 precinct in Kuala Lumpur, next to Stadium Merdeka, the museum was developed by PNB Merdeka Ventures and carries the theme 'The Malay World in Threads and Tales'.

Title: Student death probe: Kuala Kangsar boarding school instructed to give full cooperation
Article:
IPOH: The Perak Education Department has instructed a school in Kuala Kangsar to cooperate fully with police following the death of a Form Three student on its grounds today.
In a statement tonight, the department said it was closely monitoring developments surrounding the incident.
"The department has instructed the school to give its full cooperation to the police," it said.
The department also expressed its condolences to the student's family.
It said counselling and psychosocial support services had been arranged for students, teachers and school staff affected by the incident to ensure their emotional well-being was taken care of.
The department added that communication with the student's family would be handled sensitively and empathetically, with continued engagement and appropriate assistance provided.
It also urged all parties to respect the family's privacy and refrain from speculation or sharing unverified information, particularly on social media.
"This is important to protect the family's sensitivities and ensure the investigation proceeds smoothly," it said.

Title: RON97, RON95 and diesel prices drop by up to 20 sen
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The retail price of unsubsidised RON97 will drop by 20 sen per litre, while unsubsidised RON95 and diesel prices will each fall by 15 sen for the Nov 19 to 25 period.
The Finance Ministry (MOF) said in a statement that the new price of unsubsidised RON97 would be RM4 per litre, while RON95 would be RM3.72 and diesel RM4.72 per litre.
It said prices of refined petroleum products in regional markets had declined during the Automatic Pricing Mechanism (APM) calculation period, in line with the moderation of global crude oil prices.
The development reflected easing price pressures in international petroleum markets, while expectations of increased global crude oil supply had also influenced price movements.
"Supplies of petroleum products continue to increase despite several constraints that could affect market price stability.
"Geopolitical uncertainties and the risk of disruptions to petroleum shipments could still affect global supplies.
"As such, global petroleum prices are expected to remain volatile in the near term," it said.
MOF said the Madani government remained committed to protecting the public and businesses through targeted fuel subsidies under the Budi Madani initiative.
Nearly RM4 billion has been allocated for fuel subsidies next year to help ease the people's cost-of-living burden.
Under Budi95, eligible recipients will continue to enjoy RON95 at RM1.99 per litre, compared with the unsubsidised price of RM3.72.
This means the government subsidises RM1.73 per litre, or 47 per cent of the unsubsidised price.
For Budi Diesel, eligible recipients will continue paying RM2.10 per litre, compared with the unsubsidised price of RM4.72.
The government bears a subsidy of RM2.67 per litre, equivalent to 56 per cent of the unsubsidised price.
MOF said eligible Malaysians could continue purchasing subsidised RON95 and diesel using their MyKad under Budi95 and Budi Diesel, subject to their respective monthly eligibility limits.
"The Madani government will continue taking a prudent approach to protect the public from price fluctuations while ensuring the country's fuel supply remains sufficient and secure," it said.

Title: Lynas permanent disposal facility 79pct complete
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Construction of Lynas' permanent disposal facility (PDF) has reached 79 per cent as of Oct 31, the Dewan Rakyat was told.
Deputy Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk Dr Mohammad Yusof Apdal said 1.46 million metric tonnes of WLP (water leach purification) residue has been transferred into it.
"The Atomic Energy Licensing Board (AELB) is regularly monitoring construction and Lynas' compliance with its licence conditions.
"The monitoring data can also be accessed in real time through mosti.gov.my and jta.gov.my," he said when winding up the debate on his ministry's Budget 2027 allocation at the committee stage.
WLP residue is a byproduct generated during the extraction and chemical processing of rare earth elements (REEs).
On the licence, Yusof said the decision to consider a 10-year extension was subject to additional, stricter conditions, and the AELB could suspend or revoke the licence at any time in the event of non-compliance under the Atomic Energy Licensing Act.
He said that, in the first five years of the extension, Lynas was required to modify facilities at the Lynas Advanced Materials Plant in Gebeng to lower the radioactivity concentration of WLP residue below the control limit under the Act.
Lynas has submitted planning documents to modify its cracking and leaching process using the Low Temperature Leaching method, he said.
Yusof said any rare earth processing activity involving naturally occurring radioactive material above 1 becquerel per gram was subject to AELB regulation and licensing under the Act.
It was reported that Malaysia had renewed
Lynas Rare Earths
' operating licence for another 10 years to import raw materials containing naturally occurring radioactive material and process rare earths, the Australian miner said on Monday.
Shares of Lynas rose as much as seven per cent to A$20.30 by 0131 GMT, hitting their highest level since Oct 21, 2025, while the broader ASX 200 benchmark was down about 0.5 per cent.

Title: Semporna losing its edge as accommodation, dive costs climb
Article:
SEMPORNA: Rising accommodation and diving package costs are making Semporna less competitive compared with international dive destinations, says a diver from Peninsular Malaysia.
Lester Yeoh said resort stays bundled with diving packages had increased significantly, from an average of RM700 per night during the Covid-19 lockdown, when overseas travel was restricted, to between RM1,200 and RM1,500 now.
"As a diver from Peninsular Malaysia, I think prices in Semporna have gone out of hand. With that amount of money, I can get a much better experience elsewhere," he told the New Straits Times.
He said resorts offering Sipadan diving packages generally required a minimum booking of three to four nights, but guests would get only one day of diving at the world-renowned island.
"Honestly, the rest of the islands are mediocre compared with Sipadan. That is not to say there is nothing interesting.
"If you are interested in turtles, Semporna is your best bet. But, as I mentioned, it does not justify the cost," he said, adding that a return flight from Kuala Lumpur to Tawau could cost between RM600 and RM700, while a five-day, four-night holiday would cost another RM6,000.
"With RM700 for flights and another RM6,000 for the trip, I might as well go for a seven-day, six-night liveaboard in the Maldives, where I can see much more pelagic marine life, enjoy a longer holiday and experience a different culture.
"Another option is the Phuket-Similan liveaboard, which costs about RM3,000 for five days and four nights, with cheaper flights. On the final day, I can enjoy Phuket's nightlife, Thai food and traditional massage."
Yeoh said Semporna would struggle to compete with international destinations if it did not offer visitors experiences beyond marine activities.
Diving instructor Denise Lim, who has worked with a dive operator based in Semporna, concurred that the district had experienced a recent slowdown in tourism demand.
She said the dive centre was usually fully booked during the Christmas and New Year holidays, but demand had been different since last year.
Lim also expressed concern over the deterioration of Sipadan's coral reefs, attributing some of the damage to divers with poor buoyancy control.
She recalled that when she first visited the island 10 years ago, schools of jackfish and barracuda formed seemingly endless walls beneath the waters.
"My most memorable working experience as an instructor here was diving with a school of about 40 to 50 hammerhead sharks at Sipadan.
"Now, they are just a very small school," she said, urging the authorities to step up ocean protection measures and calling on divers to help protect the reefs by avoiding touching or kicking corals and using reef-safe sunscreen.
Lim, who is leaving Semporna, said the place was not perfect, particularly in terms of hygiene, but she held the place and its people dear to her heart.
